part_narrative_arc: Part I establishes the foundational architecture of Physical AI by defining the stark separation between forgiving digital computation and irreversible physical consequences across the Causal Boundary. It mathematically grounds these consequences in the severe thermodynamic and kinematic limits of the physical Body, which rigidly constrain the open-world semantic capabilities of modern neural Brains. Finally, it resolves this computational-physical tension through a deterministic Nervous System that safely arbitrates and translates statistical neural proposals into strictly bounded physical execution.

unified_case_studies.threaded_role: Introduced to demonstrate the causal boundary of mass, it becomes a quantitative subject for thermal holding-torque budgets in the Body, acts as the physical target for semantic pick-and-place proposals from the Brain, and serves as the controlled plant managed by the deterministic joint limits of the Nervous System.

Vividly illustrates unguided displacement and kinetic momentum, demonstrating why the Brain's computational latency actively consumes physical stopping distance and why the Nervous System must enforce strict watchdog lease durations bounded by clear distance.

cross_chapter_handoffs.handoff_bridge: The theoretical concept of the Causal Boundary and physical irreversibility is translated into concrete, mathematically quantifiable thermodynamic and kinematic budgets that govern the hardware.

The non-negotiable physical envelopes and actuation limits defined by the Body dictate that the high-capacity, stochastic cognitive models introduced next must operate strictly as unprivileged proposal engines.

The multi-rate, statistical policy proposals generated by the open-world Brain require a dedicated, hard real-time arbiter to safely translate them into the deterministic execution frequencies required by physical actuators.

thematic_tensions_resolved: The fundamental conflict between the stochastic, unverified nature of neural foundation models and the deterministic, safety-critical requirements of physical hardware actuation.
The contradiction between the idempotent, state-forgiving abstraction of pure software computation and the continuous, irreversible momentum and thermal realities of physical machines.
macro_threads_for_whole_book: How does the rigidly deterministic hardware anatomy and proposal-permission contract established in Part I safely acquire, process, and learn from the inherently noisy, out-of-distribution interaction data required for open-world closed-loop learning in later parts?
